course.title: Project Practicum I: Data Analytics & Machine Learning
course.description: Project Practicum 1 is a hands-on, project-based course designed to bridge the gap between theoretical machine learning knowledge and practical industry application. The course guides students through the complete lifecycle of a data science project, beginning with project ideation and the identification of specific business opportunities where machine learning can drive value. Students will learn to translate business needs into technical requirements by designing business processes and detailed technical solution architectures, including data pipelines and database schemas. The curriculum emphasizes the rigorous implementation and deployment of machine learning models, requiring students to perform exploratory data analysis (EDA), feature engineering, and hyperparameter tuning before deploying their solutions to production-ready environments using MLOps tools such as Docker and inference APIs. Finally, the course cultivates essential professional skills by requiring students to present their technical findings and project reports to stakeholders, focusing on clear communication, data storytelling, and business impact.

clos.description: Ideate and design a machine learning project that addresses a specific business need.
clos.teachingMethodsRaw: Case Study Analysis: Review successful ML use cases in industry (e.g., fraud detection, churn prediction) Use "Design Thinking" sessions to map business needs to ML tasks (Regression, Classification, etc.).
clos.assessmentMethodsRaw: Project Proposal: A formal document identifying a specific business problem and the proposed ML approach. Ideation Pitch: A short "elevator pitch" to justify why the chosen problem is suitable for an ML solution.

clos.description: Define business requirements and technical solution designs for ML models.
clos.teachingMethodsRaw: Interactive Lectures: Designing data pipelines, choosing evaluation metrics (F1-score vs. Accuracy), and selecting algorithms.
clos.assessmentMethodsRaw: Technical Design Document (TDD): A report detailing data sources, feature engineering plans, and model selection rationale. Software project should include UI/UX, Business Flowcharts, Database Entity Relationship Diagram, Use Cases, System Architecture Design, API Specifications, Technologies Usage, Mobile Devices etc.

clos.description: Implement, deploy, and evaluate a machine learning model in a production-ready environment.
clos.teachingMethodsRaw: Lab Demonstrations: Step-by-step guides on using tools like Git, Docker, Cloud ML platforms (Google Colab)
clos.assessmentMethodsRaw: End-to-end Development Pipeline & GitHub/Code Repository: Assessment of code quality, modularity, and documentation, development pipeline DEV/UAT/PROD. Performance Report: A technical evaluation of the model's performance on unseen data and its deployment latency.

clos.description: Present technical findings and project reports to stakeholders clearly.
clos.teachingMethodsRaw: Storytelling for Data Science: Workshop on how to visualize results for non-technical audiences using tools like PowerBI or Matplotlib. Mock Presentations: Practice sessions with peer feedback on delivery, body language, and clarity of complex concepts.
clos.assessmentMethodsRaw: Final Presentation: A formal presentation (demo) to a "panel of stakeholders" focusing on business impact. Reflective Report: A comprehensive project report including ethical considerations and lessons learned.

topics.title: Topic 1: Project Ideations (ML-focused)
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Identify potential real-world problems suitable for machine learning solutions. LLO2: Relate business pain points to specific ML tasks (e.g., classification, regression, clustering).

topics.title: Topic 2: Project Ideations (ML-focused)
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Assess the feasibility of proposed ML ideas based on data availability and complexity. LLO2: Select a final project topic and articulate the primary objective.

topics.title: Topic 3: Design Business Process I
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Diagram the "As-Is" (current) business process to identify inefficiencies or manual bottlenecks. LLO2: Locate specific decision points within the process where ML can intervene.

topics.title: Topic 4: Design Business Process II
topics.llosRaw: LLO2: Construct the "To-Be" (future) workflow incorporating the ML model's predictions. LLO2: Demonstrate how the new workflow improves efficiency or decision-making speed.

topics.title: Topic 5: Business Requirements
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Differentiate between functional requirements (what the model does) and non-functional requirements (latency, scalability). LLO2: Formulate success metrics (KPIs) that translate business goals into technical targets.

topics.title: Topic 6: Solutions Design I
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Deconstruct the solution into key components: data ingestion, processing, modeling, and output. LLO2: Compare different algorithms to determine the most appropriate baseline for the problem.

topics.title: Topic 7: Solutions Design II
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Design the data pipeline architecture and database schema required for the solution. LLO2: Plan the validation strategy (Train/Test/Validation split) to ensure model robustness.

topics.title: Topic 8: Implementation Phase I
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Perform exploratory data analysis (EDA) to understand data distributions and quality. LLO2: Execute data cleaning and preprocessing techniques to prepare the dataset.

topics.title: Topic 9: Implementation Phase II
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Construct feature engineering pipelines to extract relevant signals from raw data. LLO2: Train a baseline machine learning model using standard libraries (e.g., Scikit-learn, TensorFlow).

topics.title: Topic 10: Implementation Phase III
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Calibrate model hyperparameters to optimize performance metrics. LLO2: Debug model errors by analyzing confusion matrices or residual plots.

topics.title: Topic 11: Implementation Phase IV
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Validate the final model against the test set to ensure generalizability. LLO2: Assemble the final model artifacts and codebase for integration.

topics.title: Topic 12: Production Deployment & Readiness I
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Build an inference API (e.g., using Flask or FastAPI) to serve model predictions. LLO2: Containerize the application using tools like Docker for consistent deployment.

topics.title: Topic 13: Production Deployment & Readiness II
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Deploy the containerized model to a staging or cloud environment. LLO2: Test the end-to-end system for latency and reliability under load.

topics.title: Topic 14: Presentation and Reporting
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Synthesize technical complexity into clear business value propositions for stakeholders. LLO2: Defend design choices and results effectively during the final project presentation.

studentResponsibilitiesRaw: Read the learning materials beforehand which means to be ready for the next session. Be completely engaged in class, active, take notes, and ask questions in class. Students are required to participate in various activities in and out of the classroom, such as group work, and individual homework for assignments and reports assigned by the subject teacher. Submit the assigned tasks such as homework, assignments, or research proposal on time.
coursePolicyRaw: Attendance & Preparation Students are expected to attend all classes (online/on-site). Assigned readings and preparation outlines must be completed before class if any. Active participation in group discussions and post-chapter evaluations is required. Academic Integrity All assignments, quizzes, and exams must be done individually. Academic misconduct includes: - Presenting others’ work as one’s own. - Engaging in plagiarism or cheating. Homework & Assignments Preparation outlines must be submitted on time; late submissions incur penalties. Peer discussion is encouraged, but midterm and final exams must be independent. Examinations Midterm and final exams are closed-book. Penalties Violations of academic integrity may result in a failing grade and referral to the Office of Student Affairs. Students uncertain about potential violations should consult the instructor in advance.
